Welcome to Sri Lanka

Sri Lanka, a tropical gem in the Indian Ocean, basks in warm sunshine for most of the year, with seasonal monsoons occasionally refreshing its lush landscapes. With a recorded history dating back to 500 BC, this island nation is home to a vibrant tapestry of cultures — where Sinhalese, Tamil, Muslim, and Burgher communities coexist, embracing Buddhist, Hindu, Islamic, and Christian traditions.

✦

Shaped by centuries of colonial rule under the Portuguese, Dutch, and British, as well as ancient ties to India, Sri Lanka showcases a unique fusion of global influences. From centuries-old temples to colonial-era forts and the legendary leopard country of Yala, every corner of the island offers a glimpse into its rich and layered heritage, enhanced by the warmth and hospitality of its people.

01
21st April 2026 · Day 01

Airport — Colombo

B

Ayubowan! Welcome to Sri Lanka. Upon arrival at Bandaranaike International Airport, a friendly representative will greet you as you step off the aircraft and escort you to the exclusive Gold Route lounge — where you can relax, freshen up, and enjoy a refreshing cup of tea while your immigration formalities are completed and luggage collected. Your designated chauffeur then transfers you to Colombo.

Airport to Colombo · 35 km · approx. 50 minutes

Check in at the hotel for a well-deserved rest. Later in the afternoon, embark on Forgotten Colombo on a Landy — a captivating exploration of the city's lesser-known treasures aboard a classic Land Rover. Guided by an expert, you'll venture off the beaten path to discover hidden colonial architecture and vibrant local haunts, chilled drinks in hand. An intimate, private tour unlike any other.

02
22nd April 2026 · Day 02

Colombo — Cinnamon Air — Yala

AI

After breakfast, check out of the hotel and transfer to Bandaranaike International Airport. You are advised to depart the hotel by 8:45 am.

Hotel to Airport · 35 km · approx. 50 minutes

Arrive at the Cinnamon Air terminal and board your private chartered flight to Weerawila — a scenic 45-minute hop over Sri Lanka's southern heartland. On arrival at Weerawila Domestic Airport, transfer by road through the wild scrubland to the extraordinary Wild Coast Tented Lodge, perfectly positioned on the boundary of Yala National Park.

Weerawila to Yala · 30 km · approx. 1 hour

Check in, settle into your suite, and take the afternoon to explore the lodge — its pool, beachfront setting, and the sounds of the surrounding jungle setting the tone for the days ahead. This evening, enjoy your first dinner under the stars.

Should you wish to head out into the park on your first afternoon, an evening game drive departing at 3:00 pm (returning by 6:00 pm) is also available — a wonderful way to greet Yala as the heat softens and the wildlife begins to stir. Whether you choose to explore the lodge or venture into the park is entirely up to you; simply let your guide know and they will arrange the rest.

03
23rd April 2026 · Day 03

Yala National Park · Game Drive

AI

Rise early for your first guided private game drive into Yala National Park — Sri Lanka's most celebrated wildlife reserve and home to one of the world's highest concentrations of wild leopards. Your expert naturalist guide leads you through the park's diverse habitats: open grasslands, dense scrub forest, and ancient rock outcrops where leopards favour the high ground to survey their territory.

Yala is rich in birdlife, reptiles, and mammals beyond the leopard — elephants, sloth bears, water buffalo, spotted deer, and a spectacular array of waterbirds inhabit the lagoons and plains. Every drive offers something remarkable and unexpected.

An evening game drive (departing at 3:00 pm, returning by 6:00 pm) is also available — the shifting afternoon light casts Yala in a golden glow and often draws predators out as the day begins to cool. Whether you opt for one or both drives is entirely your choice; your naturalist guide will be ready whenever you are.

Return to the lodge for a leisurely afternoon — the pool, the beachfront, and the comforts of your suite await. The evening brings a shared dinner, the sounds of the wild just beyond the canvas.

04
24th April 2026 · Day 04

Yala National Park · Game Drive

AI

Another dawn, another game drive into the heart of Yala. Morning light is the finest time to encounter the park's resident elephants — family herds moving in quiet procession through the thorn scrub, calves tucked close to their mothers, the ancient social bonds of these extraordinary animals on full display. Yala hosts substantial elephant populations and close encounters are a near-daily occurrence.

Your naturalist guide reads the landscape expertly — a broken branch, a fresh track in the dust, the alarm call of a deer — piecing together the overnight movements of the park's inhabitants. Between drives, the lodge's rhythm of rest, pool time, and superb all-inclusive dining makes the day feel unhurried and deeply restorative.

An evening game drive from 3:00 pm to 6:00 pm is also on offer — Yala at dusk is a different world, with the cooling air bringing fresh activity across the plains and lagoons. You are welcome to decide on the day; there is no pressure, only possibility.

05
25th April 2026 · Day 05

Yala National Park · Game Drive

AI

Your final full day at Yala — savour every moment of the morning game drive as the park reveals its quieter, more patient face. The spotted deer that graze in the clearings at first light are a favourite sight; the stag's magnificent antlers catching the early sun as they rest in the lush green grassland, perfectly at ease in this ancient landscape.

Yala's biodiversity ensures that no two drives are alike. Whether it is a leopard draped languidly across a branch, a crocodile sunning itself on a lagoon bank, or a peacock spreading its feathers in full display, the park continues to surprise and delight at every turn.

An evening game drive (3:00 pm – 6:00 pm) offers one final opportunity to immerse yourself in Yala's magic — as the sun descends and the sky turns amber, the park takes on a stillness that is quietly breathtaking. Whether you choose to join the drive or spend the time savouring the lodge at your own pace, the choice is yours entirely.

The afternoon is yours to spend at leisure at Wild Coast — a final swim, a quiet walk along the beach, or simply sitting at the edge of the jungle as the light fades and the sounds of the night begin to rise around you.

26th April 2026 · Day 06

Yala — Cinnamon Air — Colombo · Departure

B

After an early breakfast, check out and transfer to Weerawila Domestic Airport. You are advised to depart the lodge by 8:00 am.

Yala to Weerawila · 30 km · approx. 1 hour

Board your Cinnamon Air private charter for the return flight to Colombo International Airport — approximately 45 minutes in the air, with one last view of Sri Lanka's stunning southern landscape below. On arrival, you will be escorted to the Gold Route Departure Lounge, where you will be assisted with all departure formalities — check-in, customs, and emigration — ensuring a seamless and unhurried send-off.

As your flight lifts off, carry with you the memories of leopards at dawn, elephant families at the waterhole, and the extraordinary warmth of Sri Lanka. Until we meet again — Bohoma Sthuthiyi!

Before You Go

Important Notes

Poya Days
Alcohol service at bars and restaurants is restricted on religious holidays (Poya Days) by Sri Lankan law. Please contact the hotel reception for guidance during these dates.
Check-In & Check-Out
Standard hotel check-in is at 14:00 hrs and check-out is at 12:00 hrs. Early check-in and late check-out are subject to availability and may carry additional charges.
Belongings
Hotel management will not be responsible for any belongings that are lost, stolen, or damaged during the tour. We recommend using in-room safes for valuables at all times.
Travel Times
All transfer times are approximate and subject to traffic and road conditions. The Colombo to airport transfer takes approximately 50 minutes; please allow adequate time.
Gratuities
Tips for drivers and guides are at your discretion. It is customary to express appreciation at the end of each experience — we recommend presenting gratuities personally in an envelope.
Safari & Dress
Comfortable, neutral-coloured clothing is recommended for game drives. A hat and sunscreen are essential. At religious sites, please dress modestly — cover from knees to elbows.
